I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, that is the most familiar and steady way for me to farm, and at my age I care more about reliable yield, simple field work, and easier selling than chasing a risky high-return crop. I will plant winter wheat on all my land through spring harvest, then follow with summer maize after wheat. I will use improved seed rather than expensive hybrid wheat, and hybrid maize because the yield is usually more stable for me. I will fertilize in a moderate way, not too heavy, because I want to control cost and avoid lodging and waste. I will irrigate wheat more times because spring here is often dry, while maize will get fewer irrigations unless the rain is poor. I will do rotary tillage because it fits the machinery I would use and the work is lighter than deep ploughing every season. I will spray only as much as needed for common weeds, aphids, rust, and corn borers, because I want to protect yield without overspending.
